.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r6/rules/projects/webdev-task-template/instruction.md (CHANGE_ME placeholder; no structural mandate) and environment/instructions/{integration.md,notes.md} listing
evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md (5 prose paragraphs, lines 1-9) is a firm member asking for an app: problem first (line 1 'our clients keep emailing documents to whoever answered last. We want a secure chat where each client talks to us inside their legal matter'), stated priorities (line 3 ethical walls, retention/legal hold), pointer to seed and notes plus the minimal deliverable location (line 5 /app/server.js, /app/app.db), a sign-in privacy expectation (line 7), and a request to try it in a browser before handover (line 9). grep finds no numbered/bulleted acceptance list, no shall/must spec table, no feature matrix and no framework/file-layout/endpoint list in instruction.md (the only 'must' is line 3 'they must not learn anything'). The supporting notes are first-person prose with motivations ('Our clients ask several things at once', 'Our internet in court is patchy', 'a leak is a professional-conduct problem for us'); the only table is the 5-row demo account list in walls-and-retention.md:5-11, which the skill marks as profile-expected credentials. integration.md is a runtime contract (Node 22, port 3000, DB_PATH, /api/health, fixed clock) that check 4 requires be stated, and it names no framework choice beyond preinstalled Express/better-sqlite3 and no route list besides the health path, so it is not a build recipe. Template instruction.md is only 'CHANGE_ME', so nothing template-controlled constrains this. Counterexample search: a spec-sheet rewrite (numbered 'The system shall...' list, endpoint table) would fail this row; this prompt has none of those markers. The notes are requirement-dense (e.g. the enumerated wall leak surfaces in walls-and-retention.md 'not in the matter list, the thread, search results...'), but that density is in natural voice with reasons and is relevant to rows 2/6 rather than a defect here. This is a textual row; no runtime evidence is required, and none is claimed.
